subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as public per-agent config, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 be the landing path?
rationale: The source-reproduced gap is real, but adding this config surface changes the public configuration contract plus provider/session routing behavior, which requires maintainer intent before automation should create or replace implementation work.

options.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
options.body: Approve the direction, require strict schema/docs/baseline coverage, deep-merge semantics, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof through the open PR or a narrow replacement.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` for now and defer the broader compaction/context-pruning merge surface to a later design item.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline this config expansion and close or redirect the implementation attempts, leaving users with global defaults or separate instances.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
recommendation.body: Approve the direction, require strict schema/docs/baseline coverage, deep-merge semantics, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof through the open PR or a narrow replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent compaction, runtime, docs, and config-boundary work makes this the strongest available owner signal for the product-direction decision.
